findings.problem: Stop 1, card 18 says "bless those who curse them" (Luke 6:28). "curse" gets a pop-up on this card, but "bless" does not. The only related entry is "blessed", which means "Truly happy and well off because God shows them His favor." That fits Luke 6:20-22, but not the verb in Luke 6:28, where blessing someone means wishing good on them or asking God to do them good. So the opposite of the defined word "curse" on the same card has no pop-up, and the "blessed" meaning would not help here. definitions.md says "A word always has the same meaning, so each word appears once", but it does not say what to do when a related form of a defined word ("bless" next to "blessed") has a different sense in the passage.
findings.question: Should "bless" on stop 1, card 18 get its own entry with the sense used in Luke 6:28, separate from "blessed"? Or should related forms with a different sense be left out?
